newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares seen moving sideways to lower.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares seen moving sideways to lower.

text.p: 0735 GMT - Swiss shares are expected to trade sideways to lower in a consolidation of yesterday's strong gains, dealers said. Activity was expected to be quiet as U.S. markets will remain closed today.
The focus was on Alusuisse after the company said it plans to focus its activities in six sectors and divest some businesses accounting for some 800 million Swiss francs in sales.
Dealers said market expectations ahead of the news conference, for example that Alusuisse might spin off a division, had not been met.
Alusuisse was quoted 1.4 percent lower in pre-bourse trade.
A SMI index, calculated by Bank Leu on pre-bourse prices, was 2.6 points lower at 5,802.3.

Dealers said news that Swiss retailing cooperative Migros-Genossenschafts-Bund was to buy fellow retailer Globus and that it was offering 1,180 francs per outstanding registered share and 1,080 francs per certificate will lead to switches in the sector. Funds now invested in Globus should mainly be switched to Jelmoli and maybe into Loeb shares, one trader said.
* The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 12.84 points, or 0.35 percent, to 3,668.36.
* Novartis registered shares, which shot up four percent on Thursday, were up 12 francs to 2,461.

* Alusuisse shares were prominent losers after the company at today's news conference dashed hopes that it would announce a spin-off of a division. Alusuisse registered shares fell 37 francs, or 3.78 percent, to 1,471.
* Banks and insurers were mostly mixed.
* Shares of Swiss Life slid 10 francs to 579 after posting strong gains on Thursday, its first trading day.
* Stocks of Swiss retailers Globus jumped 28 percent to 1,150.
Earlier, Swiss retailing cooperative Migros said it was to buy Globus and that it was offering 1,180 francs per outstanding registered share and 1,080 francs per certificate.
* Jelmoli added 20 francs to 1,020. Dealers said after Globus would be taken over, switches were likely into Jelmoli.
